depRef:
| method | caller | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `infra.apply` (POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | Distils, checks, holds, tests, deploys and removes Workers. The sections below give each step. |
| `infra.getState` (GET) | the owner's session, the recovery key | The Workers, their probation, the confirmed versions, the held deploys and the approvals that stand. |
| `infra.approvalRequests`, `infra.approvalRequest`, `infra.approveRequest` | see Asking the owner | The requests of held deploys. |
| `infra.confirm` (POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | Ends the probation of one Worker. |
| `infra.redistil` (POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | Distils the kept source of every Worker again with this deployer. With `apply: true` it deploys each Worker whose code changes. |
| `infra.tokenWorkers` (GET, POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | The Workers that a sign-in link's token may change. |
| `infra.canaryKey` (GET, POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | The SHA-256 of the canary key. See The canary key. |
| `infra.reviewKey` (GET, POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | The SHA-256 of the review key. See The review key. |
| `infra.shell` (POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | Passes the body to brain-static as `shell/index.html`, or with `?name=verify` as `shell/verify.html`. Both files are public. |
| `infra.distil` (POST) | the owner's session, the recovery key | Answers what a source distils to. It deploys nothing. |
| `infra.exportRows`, `infra.importRows`, `infra.rowsDigest` | the recovery key | See Moving to a new Worker name. |
| `infra.getModules` (GET) | anyone | The source of each module of a Worker of this Brain, and cloudflare-iac. `?dry=ID` gives the modules of that dry apply in place of the kept ones. |
| `member.deploy`, `member.remove`, `member.modules` | the kernel, for a member | See A member's Worker. |
| `member.purge` | the kernel, for the owner | Removes every Worker of one member. |
The installer deploys `deployer_service`, and nothing on the Brain can change it: `deployerAllows` and the role check in `refusal` refuse any apply that names it. Its cron calls `tick` once a minute. Its `calls` names `blob.upload`, for the docs of a service (see Docs of a service). The core checks `calls` only for a Worker known by its key, not for the deployer, so the list says what the deployer may call and gates nothing; brain-x-blob decides on the caller `deployer`.

| the run gave | the deployer | the result's `state` | log line |
|---|---|---|---|
| a pass for the hash that runs | ends the probation and tells the core (`deploy.report`) | `verified`, `tests`, `run` | `deploy.verified` |
| a fail for the hash that runs, with a version before | puts the version before back at once and opens an issue (below) | `put-back`, `previous`, `reason`, `failures: [{ test }]`, `run` | `deploy.failed`, `deploy.put-back` with `run` |
| a fail, and no version before | leaves the version running, tells the core, and opens an issue | `failing`, `failed`, `failures`, `run` | `deploy.failed` |
| a verdict for another hash | nothing | the state of the deploy | `deploy.verify.stale` |
| no verdict: no browser, no time bought, the wait passed, or the page could not judge | nothing | the state of the deploy | `deploy.verify.none` with the reason |
| the run gave | fields of the answer |
|---|---|
| a pass | `tests`, `ms`; `state` stays `ready` or `unchanged` |
| a fail | `state: "tests-failed"`, `tests`, `failed: [{ name, message, stack }]`, `reason`, `ms` |
| no verdict, or a verdict for another hash | `none` with the reason; `state` stays |
| the apply gave | the answer for the entry |
|---|---|
| the page holds the new text after the write | `state: "verified"` (or the Worker's `deployed` or `probation`), `tests`, `ms`, `shared` |
| the page held the new text before the apply | the Worker's state, `shared` |
| a dry apply with passing tests | `state: "ready"` (or the Worker's state), `tests`, `ms`, `shared` |
| failed tests | `state: "tests-failed"` as in A dry run runs the tests; the page stays as it is |
| no verdict, a write that does not reach the page, or a page that changed after the read | `state: "not-stored"` with `reason`; the page stays as it is. A dry apply with no verdict answers `none` and keeps the state. |
| field | holds |
|---|---|
| `docs` | the manifest of the docs after the change: NAME.md to `{ sha256, size }` |
| `wasDocs` | the manifest the caller synced, before the change |
| `docText` | NAME.md to text, for each doc whose sha256 differs from `wasDocs` |
| step | what | check |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Update `BASE-guard` in place to this module, so that it has `exportRows`. | `infra.getState` answers as before |
| 2 | Install `BASE-deployer` with the same recovery key and `config.self`. Send it the rows of the old one. | `infra.rowsDigest` is equal on both |
| 3 | Install `BASE-guard` again with `config.replacedBy`. It then changes nothing: no apply, no tick, no approval. | an apply to it answers 409 `Replaced` |
| 4 | Apply every service through `BASE-deployer`. The kernel and the core then bind it as `DEPLOYER`. | every Worker is `same` under `redistil` |
| 5 | Put a stub on `BASE-guard` with no Cloudflare token and no recovery key. Its rows stay. | its bindings are `ROWS` and `BRAIN_CONFIG` |
| | |
|---|---|
| Name | `brain-m-ID-NAME`. `ID` is the first ten hex digits of the SHA-256 of the member's DID. `NAME` is the name given to `cloudflare.Service`, 1 to 20 lower case letters and digits. A recipe cannot have a name `brain-x-m-…`, and a system Worker cannot have a name `brain-m-…`. |
| Source | The deployer distils it in QuickJS, with no other module's kept source. The source has at most 200,000 characters and the code at most 1,000,000. The sandbox stops a source that does not end (see `distilIn` in `cloudflare-iac`). |
| What the deployer takes from the distil | The code, the Worker's name, and for each method its type and `who`. The deployer writes the bindings, the role, the flags and the rules itself. |
| Bindings | `CORE`, its own key, `BRAIN_CONFIG` and its manifest. No database, no bucket, no secret, no other Worker. |
| Platform cells | `sql` and `xrpc`. The deployer refuses any other, and a secret, a path, a cron, a flag, a tail and Cloudflare permissions. |
| Methods | Named `com.lopecode.brain.m.ID.…`. `who` is `"author"` (the member, and the owner) or `"members"` (any signed-in member, and the owner). |
| Address | None: its `workers.dev` address is off, and the core asks it for its health. |
| Limit | 3 Workers a member, or the number the owner set for them. 60 calls of `member.deploy` a member an hour, or the owner's number. The count is under `mdeploys/DID/HOUR`, before the distil. A call that the deployer refuses, or that changes nothing, counts. |
| Name held | Two DIDs can share an `ID`. The deployer refuses a deploy to a name that holds a Worker of another member. |
| Source kept | Under `msource/`, apart from the modules that `infra.getModules` lists. `member.modules` answers `cloudflare-iac` and the calling member's modules, for a page served to that member. |
